title: Garlic Turkey Skillet
shortDescription: One-pan seasoned turkey with peppers, corn, and melted cheese
subtitle: One-pan seasoned turkey with peppers, corn, and melted cheese
description: Lean ground turkey browns with taco seasoning, bell pepper, corn, and black beans, finished with melted cheddar for scooping into tortillas or bowls.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Turkey Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch turkey. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown turkey
steps.instruction: Cook ground turkey in a large skillet over medium-high 8–10 minutes, breaking into fine crumbles until no pink remains and edges look lightly browned. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.instruction: Stir in onion and bell pepper. Cook 5–6 minutes until softened and onion turns translucent with slightly softened pepper pieces. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season and simmer
steps.instruction: Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, corn, beans, tomatoes, and salt. Simmer 8 minutes until liquid reduces and mixture looks thick, not soupy. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Melt cheese
steps.instruction: Remove from heat, sprinkle cheddar evenly, cover 2 minutes until cheese melts into a glossy layer on top. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Scoop into tortillas or bowls. Turkey should stay moist with visible corn and pepper pieces throughout each portion. Plan about 2 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Add a splash of lime at the end—acid lifts turkey from bland to bright.
Offer Greek yogurt as a cool topping instead of sour cream.
Double recipe fits two skillets for faster browning on busy nights.
tonightSpread: Warm flour tortillas and shredded lettuce.
leftovers: Taco salad over romaine with crushed baked chips.
Stuffed into bell pepper halves and baked 15 minutes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: High protein, low grease, and one pan to wash. Familiar taco flavors without frying shells.
mealPrepNotes: Pre-measure taco spice blend. Open and drain beans before the call comes in. Station: Use a 14-inch skillet or two 12-inch pans so turkey browns instead of steaming. Station: Add cheese off heat so it melts without oil separating at the edges. Station: Serve straight from skillet to warm tortillas at the adjacent counter.
